confirmed: Read all 28,500 characters of the markdown in contiguous chunks, extracted text from all 16 PDF pages, and visually inspected the embedded Table 1, Table 2, Figure 1, and Figure 2 images that the markdown omitted. The PDF ends with references and has no appended supplement (PDF pp. 14-16).

The source is Research Square v2, posted June 20th, 2025, DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-6937665/v2; title and authors match the form, including the document spelling Oliver Rittman. The file contains 16 PDF pages, with printed pages 1-14 on PDF pages 3-16 (PDF pp. 1-2 and page footers).

The Crossref primary record for DOI 10.2139/ssrn.5313034 has the same title and author sequence, with Rittmann rather than the PDF spelling Rittman, supporting the SSRN bibliographic match. Only Crossref metadata for SSRN was read; all study findings were checked in the local Research Square PDF (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2139%2Fssrn.5313034).

One randomized people study is present: researchers were individually assigned, after stratification, to unrestricted GPT access or a no-AI control while revising their own manuscripts at a Mannheim research hackathon. Field RCT is supported; expert-rated originality supplies an output-scored novelty outcome, so has_randomized_people_study is true and the paper belongs in randomized-study checking despite its small sample (PDF p. 3, Introduction; PDF pp. 5-6, Participants and Design, Intervention and Writing Task, and Faculty Expert Assessments).

The assignment passage explicitly says twenty-two participants were randomized, and Statistical Analyses gives n=22. These counts refer to people, not manuscripts or ratings; no separate attrition count is reported. The form correctly retains 22 randomized and 22 as the stated analysis sample, with no per-arm numerical count inferred from the phrase two equal groups (PDF p. 3, Introduction; PDF p. 5, Participants and Design; PDF p. 8, Statistical Analyses).

The study remains below the codebook threshold of 50 analyzed people: core=no, criterion 1=met, criterion 2=not_met, criterion 3=met, and context_class=none are correct. It is a small randomized experiment rather than observational, synthesis, or AI-versus-human-output context (PDF pp. 3, 5-6, 8; creativity-codebook.md, sections 3-4).

The discipline counts match exactly: political science 14, sociology 2, economics 2, psychology 2, finance 1, and policy analysis 1. Only two participants were native English speakers (PDF p. 5, Participants and Design and footnote 2; PDF p. 3, Introduction).

The abstract identifies GPT-4; the intervention section says the commercial version of ChatGPT or any AI tool. The event lasted three days, used two-hour writing sessions, and offered both groups an optional eight-week revision window (PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 5-6, Intervention and Writing Task).

Five expert evaluators scored six manuscript dimensions on a 5-point Likert scale, from 1=very poor to 5=excellent, while blind to treatment group but aware of pre/post status. The outcome is the post-minus-pre change in ratings; these raters and ratings do not add to the participant count (PDF p. 6, Evaluation Procedures: Faculty Expert Assessments).

S1-O1 reported string matches exactly: Table 1 Originality estimate 0.11; t, unclustered 0.58; t, clustered 0.27; t, stratified and clustered 0.61; Westfall-Young adjusted p 0.87. The prose separately prints estimate=0.114, p=0.875; retain both as printed (PDF p. 8, Table 1 image; PDF p. 10, Results).

S1-O2 reported string matches exactly: Table 1 Clarity estimate 0.49; t, unclustered 2.29; t, clustered 1.99; t, stratified and clustered 2.61; Westfall-Young adjusted p 0.01. The prose prints estimated effect=0.486, adjusted p=0.009 (PDF p. 8, Table 1 image; PDF p. 9, Results).

S1-O3 reported string matches exactly: Table 1 Coherence estimate 0.43; t, unclustered 1.84; t, clustered 1.77; t, stratified and clustered 2.29; Westfall-Young adjusted p 0.04. The prose prints estimated effect=0.427, adjusted p=0.036 (PDF p. 8, Table 1 image; PDF p. 9, Results).

The Table 1 estimates are raw Likert-scale treatment effects on changes in ratings, not standardized effect sizes or pooled synthesis estimates. The synthesis fields appropriately remain empty (PDF p. 6, Faculty Expert Assessments; PDF p. 8, Table 1 caption).

The paper points to https://osf.io/f4epg for the preregistration and supplemental materials and states that replication materials include Python files for the SakanaAI analysis. The supplement is not included in the local PDF; its contents and any supplement-only statistics were not independently retrieved (PDF p. 3, footnote 1; PDF p. 7, footnote 3).

The reflective-writing analysis concerns linguistic markers of thought processes, and the human-versus-AI assessor comparison concerns rating methods; neither establishes a separate randomized participant study, an across-person diversity outcome, or an unassisted creative-performance outcome after AI removal (PDF p. 7, Analysis of Self-Reflective Writing; PDF pp. 10-12, Figures 1-2 and associated Results).
summary: The PDF confirms a randomized field study of 22 researchers, below the 50-person threshold, and all recorded statistics match. Corrections concern company involvement, omitted outcomes and AI-rating details, incomplete preregistration/outcome coding, and wording that overstates the null originality result.
